chunks: Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim narrated from Abu Abdullah, from his forefathers, from Ali عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ruled regarding the floodwaters of the Valley of Mahzur that the upper land should retain the water over the lower land: for crops until it reaches the level of the sandal strap, and for palm trees until it reaches the ankle; then the water should be released to the lower land beyond that.

key_terms.الشِّرَاكِ: the level of the sandal strap, a measure for water depth
key_terms.الْكَعْبِ: the ankle, a measure for water depth
key_terms.سَيْلِ: floodwater or flowing runoff used for irrigation
key_terms.وَادِي مَهْزُورٍ: the Valley of Mahzur, the location of the ruling
key_terms.يُحْبَسَ: to be retained or held back temporarily

ai.seo_question: How did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم rule on distributing irrigation water between upper and lower lands?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم concerning the fair distribution of floodwater between upper and lower lands in Wadi Mahzur. It establishes measured upstream use for irrigation before releasing the water downstream, reflecting justice in shared water rights and agricultural usage.
